Job Description
The Semiconductor Manufacturing Director leads and oversees all operational aspects of a semiconductor manufacturing facility, driving the efficient and effective production of high-quality semiconductor products. This strategic leadership position demands deep expertise in semiconductor manufacturing processes, coupled with strong technical and business acumen. Success in this role requires exceptional communication skills and proven management capabilities to guide teams, optimize operations, and deliver excellence in a dynamic, technology-driven environment.
Key Responsibilities:
Workflow Coordination: Track production progress against schedules, promptly identifying and addressing bottlenecks or inefficiencies.
Resource Allocation: Manage the effective deployment of labor, materials, and equipment to meet production targets, coordinating with supply chain and logistics teams to prevent shortages.
Scheduling: Dynamically adjust production schedules to accommodate shifting priorities, equipment maintenance needs, or urgent orders.
Quality Assurance: Implement rigorous quality procedures to reduce human error and minimize defects, working closely with the Quality Control team to execute corrective actions.
Safety Leadership: Enforce strict health and safety regulations, conducting regular audits, identifying hazards, and fostering a culture of safety through ongoing training and proactive risk management.
5S Culture: Drive the integration of 5S protocols into daily routines to improve workplace organization and efficiency, leading periodic 5S audits and continuous improvement training.
People Management: Lead a team of supervisors and operators by setting clear priorities, conducting performance reviews, and serving as a role model through a strong work ethic and adherence to procedures.
Skill Development: Identify skill gaps within the team and design targeted training programs to strengthen technical and soft skills, ultimately reducing labor turnover.
Performance Coaching: Provide consistent feedback and coaching to help employees meet and exceed productivity and quality goals.
Strategic Problem-Solving: Quickly troubleshoot production issues related to equipment, materials, or workflow to minimize downtime.
Operational Efficiency: Continuously evaluate production processes to reduce cycle times, eliminate waste, and optimize costs while maintaining quality standards.
Data-Driven Reporting: Maintain accurate records of output, quality, and attendance, providing management with regular updates and data-backed recommendations for operational improvements.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with Engineering, Maintenance, and Quality teams to implement new technologies or processes, ensuring alignment with broader company initiatives.
This Job Is For You If:
Develop and implement strategic plans to achieve business objectives, improve manufacturing efficiency, and reduce costs
Lead and manage a team of senior managers, engineers, and technicians to ensure alignment with company goals
Oversee the entire semiconductor manufacturing process, including wafer fabrication, assembly, and test
Ensure compliance with quality, safety, and environmental regulations and standards
Implement and maintain lean manufacturing principles and continuous improvement methodologies
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to resolve technical issues, improve yields, and optimize manufacturing processes
Develop and implement quality control and assurance processes to ensure high-quality products
Manage relationships with suppliers, ensuring timely delivery of high-quality materials and equipment
Oversee inventory management, minimizing waste and optimizing inventory levels
Develop and manage budgets, forecasts, and cost reduction initiatives
Analyze financial performance and make data-driven decisions to optimize manufacturing operations
Attract, retain, and develop top talent in the semiconductor manufacturing industry
Foster a culture of innovation, collaboration, and continuous learning
Job Requirements
Must Have:
Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, Industrial Engineering, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant direct work experience.
Minimum of 10 years of experience in semiconductor manufacturing, including at least 5 years in a leadership capacity.
Demonstrated track record of successfully managing complex manufacturing operations while driving improvements in efficiency and cost reduction.
Demonstrated proficiency in Lean manufacturing principles, including Kaizen and 5S methodologies.
Exceptional leadership capabilities with the ability to manage diverse teams and drive cultural change.
Strong analytical skills with the ability to translate production data into actionable operational strategies.

sourceEvidence.quote:
Job Description
BAE Systems is hiring a Director I – Strategic Operations to support our Maritime Solutions business in Jacksonville, FL. The Director leads Production Craft Managers and Supervisors to achieve company goals, specifically safety and delivery of projects under budget and on-time while maintaining quality and relationships. The Director leads the production crafts at the Jacksonville Shipyard; directly managing and coordinating production activities, production shops, and related facilities and resources. The role will develop, maintain, and direct all aspects of the Jacksonville Production Craft Managers and Supervisors.

Responsibilities:
  • Leads the production crafts that directly support the Operations Department and shipyard business objectives.
  • Maintains a strategic view of craft performance and evaluates overall staffing-level requirements consistent with the business plan and projected changes in work volume.
  • Work with Planning, PMO, and Operations to build accurate schedules, budgets, and staffing plans that are used to monitor, control, and adjust workflows as the projects progress.
  • Supports the estimating and planning phases of projects by providing accurate trade estimates and execution strategy with profitable capture of projects as primary objective.
  • Participates in reviews and analysis of projects in execution, ensuring schedule and cost objectives are being achieved or appropriate corrective actions initiated.
  • Continually monitors performance of projects in execution, to include review of Cost Performance Index (CPI), Schedule Performance Index (SPI), Estimated Time to Completion (ETC), and Estimated Actual Completion (EAC) on product lines.
  • Seeks continuous improvements utilizing historical data to achieve improved performance.
  • Take timely and appropriate action to ensure all cost, quality, and schedule criteria are met and overall performance is improved.
  • Develops accurate, concise changes in scope of base work package and as found conditions by initiating/writing the CFR to describe the problem.
  • Reports and leads corrective action on production technical problems that are design and/or manufacturing in nature.
  • Removes roadblocks identified by Production Supervisors, Area Managers, and Production workers.
  • Provides direction regarding shop investment, process improvement, and training.
  • Ensures proper staffing by analyzing the business plan, forecasting the craft personnel and craft management necessary to achieve the shipyard business objectives effectively and efficiently, and continually adjusting and maintaining the required levels of both.
  • Creates a business culture where people are valued and engaged.
  • Participates in talent attraction and acquisition activities including supporting hiring events, conducting interviews, and contributing to hiring decisions.
  • Manages employee performance and takes appropriate action regarding salary increases, promotions, mentoring, training, disciplining, etc.
  • Drives ethical behavior and instills a culture of Safety, Health, and Environmental (SHE) excellence throughout the production workforce.
  • Champions continuous improvement of Safety processes and compliance with SHE objectives and policies.
  • Promote programs and process such as, PPE, stretch and flex, housekeeping, discussing job hazard analysis, and accident prevention.
  • Leads and influences organizational transformation and change to drive the mission forward, continuously improve, and optimize a diverse workforce.


Required Education, Experience, & Skills
  • Bachelor's Degree and 12 years of work experience or equivalent experience
  • Experience in Program/Operations Management
  • Experience in People Management/Leadership
  • Experience in Marine/Maritime, Shipbuilding/Ship Repair
  • Experience in planning, scheduling, budgeting, estimating, resource allocation, risk and opportunity management
  • Knowledge of shipyard production procedures, ship repair methods, and related government regulations and administrative procedures
  • Knowledge of shipyard craft operations related to machinery, tooling, safety, etc.
  • Ability to develop and implement strategic plans
  • Ability to schedule, direct, and organize work within a diverse department and coordinate cross-functionally to maintain efficiency
  • Ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines effectively
  • Ability to work within a dynamic environment and respond well to last minute, high priority, time sensitive projects
  • Ability to handle the pressure of constant interruptions
  • Ability to interface and communicate with all levels of internal and external stakeholders
  • Ability to lead, coach, mentor, and motivate employees in an evolving production environment
  • Ability to facilitate group decision-making, team building, and conflict resolution
  • Ability to research problem areas and special requests
  • Ability to react and perform in emergency situations
  • Self-starter that is well-organized, detail-oriented, and customer-focused
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
  • Strong communication and presentation skills


Preferred Education, Experience, & Skills
  • Advanced Degree in Engineering, Project Management, Business, Finance, or similar
  • Experience in US Navy Defense Ship Repair
  • Experience in Change Management and Continuous Improvement
  • Knowledge of OSHA and Environmental regulations
  • Ability to understand work specifications, work orders, blueprints, contracts, and technical publications
  • Ability to support growth initiatives, business development strategies, proposal development, and contract negotiations
  • Ability to lead workforce development, training, upskilling, reskilling, etc.
  • Ability to participate in diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging (DEIB) initiatives
  • Comfortable working in an industrial shipyard environment




Pay Information
Full-Time Salary Range: $153377 - $260743

Please note: This range is based on our market pay structures. However, individual salaries are determined by a variety of factors including, but not limited to: business considerations, local market conditions, and internal equity, as well as candidate qualifications, such as skills, education, and experience.

Employee Benefits: At BAE Systems, we support our employees in all aspects of their life, including their health and financial well-being. Regular employees scheduled to work 20+ hours per week are offered: health, dental, and vision insurance; health savings accounts; a 401(k) savings plan; disability coverage; and life and accident insurance. We also have an employee assistance program, a legal plan, and other perks including discounts on things like home, auto, and pet insurance. Our leave programs include paid time off, paid holidays, as well as other types of leave, including paid parental, military, bereavement, and any applicable federal and state sick leave. Employees may participate in the company recognition program to receive monetary or non-monetary recognition awards. Other incentives may be available based on position level and/or job specifics.


About BAE Systems, Inc.
BAE Systems, Inc. is a defense, aerospace, and security company headquartered in Falls Church, Virginia, with more than 40,000 employees worldwide. We serve, supply, and protect those who protect us. As one of the most geographically diverse international defense companies, we deliver a full range of products and services spanning air, land, maritime, space, and cyber, including advanced electronics, intelligence solutions, and dedicated customer support.

Our culture is performance-driven and values-led, built on curiosity, creativity, and collaboration. Purpose isn't a tagline here. It's what drives us. We're developing breakthrough technologies that defend national security and make a lasting impact on our communities and our planet. When you join BAE Systems, you're not just building a career. You're contributing to a mission that truly matters.

This position will be posted for at least 5 calendar days. The posting will remain active until the position is filled, or a qualified pool of candidates is identified.

You will translate electro-optical and system requirements into manufacturable module designs, supplier process controls, incoming/EOL test coverage, and line-ready build instructions. You will lead NPI gates, yield and cosmetic defect reduction, second-source and capacity ramps, and field/factory issue closure with CIS vendors, module makers, Manufacturing, Quality, and Supply Chain. Own end-to-end implementation of image sensor and camera-module designs into production: DFM/DFA, stack-up freeze, BOM readiness, build documentation, and release criteria for NPI through HVM
Industrialize sensor/module processes with module manufacturers and internal lines—die attach, wirebond/flip-chip, active alignment, lens/barrel assembly, filter/cover glass, sealing, and cure profiles—driving Cp/Cpk, scrap reduction, and cycle-time targets
Define production test and inspection strategy (wafer/probe correlation where applicable, module EO test, cosmetic AOI, functional/EOL, burn-in or stress screens as required); set guardbands, golden samples, and MSA for factory metrology
Establish and maintain EO and image-quality specs that are factory-executable: QE/response, noise, defective pixels, PRNU, black level, HDR/flicker behavior, multi-camera matching—balanced for perception needs and manufacturing yield
Lead yield, defect, and process excursions: Pareto analysis, DOE on assembly and test, root-cause with FA (optical, electrical, physical), and permanent corrective actions into supplier control plans and Tesla work instructions
Drive automotive-grade qualification and production validation for sensors/modules (TC, THB/HAST, mechanical shock/vibe, solar/UV load, life tests); lock process change management (PCN) and requalification triggers
Partner with Manufacturing Engineering, Test Engineering, and Quality on line bring-up, takt and capacity models, traceability, and containment playbooks for factory and field escapes
Manage CIS and camera-module supplier industrialization programs: process capability audits, dual-source enablement, cost-down without quality regression, and ramp readiness for new vehicle launches
Resolve implementation issues at the system boundary—thermal, EMI, flex/PCB interface, connector/sealing, contamination, stray light introduced by assembly tolerances—and feed learnings into next-gen designs
Mentor implementation and camera manufacturing engineers; standardize playbooks for sensor NPI, factory metrics dashboards, and cross-program industrialization best practices

Degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Optics, Physics, Manufacturing Engineering, or related field, or equivalent practical experience. Industrialization track record outweighs pure research pedigree
8+ years (12+ years preferred) bringing CMOS image sensors and/or camera modules from prototype into high-volume manufacturing—automotive, mobile, industrial machine vision, or similar high-reliability volume products

Hands-on experience with module assembly processes (active alignment, bonding, sealing, optical stack) and factory quality systems (control plans, FMEA, SPC, 8D, traceability)

Own industrialization strategy across camera platforms, unblock multi-site ramps, dual-source critical sensors/modules, and raise the manufacturing bar for imaging hardware
Bias to the factory floor and supplier lines; willingness to travel to module makers and Tesla manufacturing sites as needed (often 25%+ during ramps)

About Foundational
Foundational is building a network of AI-native, autonomous factories for modern contract manufacturing — reshoring critical supply chains so companies can produce high-quality products domestically, quickly, and at competitive cost. Recent breakthroughs in robotics and physical AI have shifted autonomous manufacturing from theoretical to deployable, and we're focused on operationalizing these capabilities at scale during a decisive decade for American industrial leadership.
WHO — Who Thrives Here
At Foundational, we're building with people who want to own something — to do work that matters, in an environment where what you ship is what counts.
The people who thrive here:
Take ownership before they're asked. They see the gap and close it.
Operate with a high degree of judgment. We move fast, and good judgment travels farther than a playbook.
Communicate directly — concise, clear, and candid, especially when stakes are high.
Hold a high bar for themselves first, then for everyone around them.
Are genuinely energized by hard problems in physical, real-world environments. Energized — not just interested.
Stay effective when things are ambiguous, changing, or under pressure. That's the job.
This is a place for people who want to build something that has never existed before and leave a clear mark on it.
MISSION
This person owns the quality system that earns Foundational the right to build — across every vertical we serve and every standard our customers run on. Without it, we don’t pass first audit, we don’t win regulated programs, and our customers can’t ship.
OUTCOMES — What Success Looks Like in 6–12 Months
We track results. Here's what we expect this person to own and deliver:
Stand up a single QMS that serves every vertical Foundational builds in — architected from day one to absorb the toughest standards (AS9100, ISO 13485, IATF 16949, ISO 9001) so layering on additional certifications and customer-specific requirements is a configuration step, not a rebuild.
Own the certification roadmap end-to-end — ISO 9001 as the baseline, then the vertical-specific standards our first programs require (AS9100, ISO 13485, IATF 16949, NADCAP, and others as the customer mix demands) — and pass each audit on the first attempt.
Build supplier quality from zero — qualification, FAIs, PPAP where required, source inspection, and counterfeit-mitigation controls aligned to AS9100 / AS6171.
Establish the operating cadence that keeps quality real on the floor — control plans, FAIs, in-process inspection, NCR/CAPA discipline, MRB, SPC, and the closed-loop feedback that drives yield and cost of poor quality down every quarter.
Define the digital QMS — document control, training records, NCR/CAPA, audit, supplier quality — and partner with engineering so traceability and inspection data are software-native, not paper retrofitted into a database.
SKILLS
Multi-standard QMS architecture — deep fluency in ISO 9001, AS9100, ISO 13485 / FDA QSR (21 CFR 820), and IATF 16949, and a working sense of where they converge, where they don’t, and how additional customer- and vertical-specific standards layer on top
Audit leadership — registrar, customer, and regulatory; you’ve led companies through first-time certification and passed cleanly
Core quality engineering toolkit — APQP/PPAP, FMEA, control plans, MSA, SPC, 8D, root cause and CAPA discipline that actually closes loops
Electronics & precision-manufacturing quality — IPC-A-610 / J-STD-001, FAIs (AS9102), source inspection, dimensional metrology, and special-process accreditation (NADCAP)
Digital QMS & data fluency — comfortable defining the systems and data model (eQMS, traceability, inspection records) that the function runs on, not just operating off a shared drive
COMPETENCIES
These are the behavioral patterns that predict success here — in practice, under pressure.
Accountability
— You own outcomes. If something's off track, you say so and fix it.
Bias for action
— You ship. You iterate. You move toward the hard thing.
Clarity of communication
— Direct and concise, especially when it counts.
Learning agility
— You get up to speed fast in unfamiliar territory.
Resilience
— You stay sharp when things are hard, ambiguous, or moving fast.
High standards
— You raise the bar rather than match it — and hold yourself to it first.
Building from zero
— You can stand up a quality system from scratch — documents, processes, certifications, the team — and run it yourself until there’s a team to hand it off to.

This is a filter as much as it is an invitation.We're turning reindustrialization from a talking point into an operating reality. The work is hard, the environment is demanding, and the stakes are real. We compensate with base, bonus, and equity to reflect impact, responsibility, and results, with meaningful upside for the people who help build and scale this company.
For those aligned with the mission and motivated by execution at scale, Foundational offers the opportunity to help define one of the most consequential industrial transformations of the next decade.

Actively create/sustain a strong talent management process and committee for all people. Create a dynamic learning culture in which people grow within and beyond the facility
Think strategically and systematically; work towards long-term success, as well as facilities’ short-term success
Problem solve and make decisions by applying analytical and creative thinking skills, as well as strong business and sense of urgency
Complete face-to-face reviews and individual development plans with staff-level employees annually
Ensure that meetings are transparent, candid, constructive, and overall up-lifting. Connects what the people are doing to success and their customer’s success
Actively support and participate in the application of organizational principles, tools, and processes (i.e., layered process audits) creating an environment in which the plant principles and tools thrive.
Review income statement daily. Adjust staffing, approve salaried overtime, and discretionary spending plans as required to flex with volume.
Monthly review and sign off on forecasts including income statement, and balance sheet.
Lead budgeting/AOP process at plant level
Lead plant-level review of operating metrics once a month.
Review and sign off on capital and startup costs in quotes.
Review weekly trend before submitting to finance.
Support Quality Management Team to ensure compliance to client quality systems.
Ensure key quality metrics are reviewed daily covering customer quality performance, manufacturing process driven scrap, and significant impacts to FTT performance as per guidance in Operating System standards.
Support Operations Team in ensuring completion per assigned plant schedule.
Ensure monthly management reviews, including quality metrics, customer scorecard performance, cost of poor quality, and review of product launch/safe launch activity.
Support and ensure cooperation between departments in addressing issues.
Drive production to ensure delivery of customer requirements is met. Communicate any issues and action to resolve.
Review capacity at least quarterly; constraints in capacity should be escalated.
Review and approve any premium freight.
Review inventory performance on a weekly basis.
What Qualifications You Should Have
Bachelor’s degree in engineering or Business-Related Field preferred.
Minimum of 7+ years of progressively more responsible supervisory / managerial and leadership experience in high volume manufacturing operation (Automotive experience required).
Strong communication skills, performance, and proficiency management, staffing management, time management, coordination, training, financial planning, efficient in standards development, sound in decision making and strategic management.
Excellent understanding of continuous improvement concepts including Six Sigma, Lean, value stream mapping, etc.

Summary
Leads the Site Quality organization in developing and executing a quality strategy, ensuring achievement of goals in alignment with the site, corporate and customer requirements.
Detailed Description
Performs tasks such as, but not limited to, the following:
Assesses and ensures mitigation of organizational risk in regards to Quality events or potential events
Has overall responsibility for planning, budgeting, implementing and maintaining costs, methods and resources including employees in the quality function
Leads the organization in developing and executing a Quality strategy that ensures long term customer satisfaction, site and corporate goals are achieved or exceeded, including regular reviews on progress
Provides direct and indirect leadership and mentorship to subordinate managers and employees for effective development and execution of skills such as Leadership Development, Problem Solving 8D Methodology, Compliance Procedures, Change Control Board, FMEA, Manufacturing Quality Standards (MQS) and Flawless Launch Phase Gate Reviews.
Develops and conduct reviews with key customer and suppliers to ensure that quality requirements are aligned and achieving defined level of customer satisfaction and managing any associated contractual LD risks
Provides leadership and support for compliance readiness to various customer, regulatory standards and certifications (i.e ISO9001, TL9001, AS9100, ISO13485, ISO14001, ANSI/ESD, etc.)
Collaborates with site leadership to support the activities necessary to achieve Celestica Operating System processes and metrics and ensure on going development of a Quality culture

Excellent knowledge of quality management systems and processes (i.e ISO9001, TL9001,
AS9100, ISO13485, ISO14001, ANSI/ESD, etc.)
Broad knowledge of an electronic manufacturing environment, materials, manufacturing and business processes.
Excellent analytical, negotiation and problem resolution skills.
Ability to establish department goals and coordinate a wide variety of resources to meet quality and quantity metrics.
Ability to evaluate, prioritize and problem solve a variety of tasks to ensure their timely and accurate completion.
Ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing, with a wide variety of internal and external customers.

Ability to define and manage large multi departmental change process's to project objectives

Bachelor's degree in related field or consideration of an equivalent combination of education and experience
